title: gate the unwritable-trust-file test behind cfg(unix) so the Windows suite compiles
action: The Windows CI job fails to COMPILE, not to assert: preflight_warns_and_proceeds_when_the_file_is_unwritable in packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/herding/run.rs (around line 4481) imports std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt and calls Permissions::from_mode, neither of which exists on Windows, so the whole test binary is a build error there (E0433 plus two E0599 at run.rs:4482, 4489, 4495) and every other Windows test in that crate goes unrun. The test proves a mode-0o500 directory makes the atomic write fail, which has no Windows equivalent. Put #[cfg(unix)] directly above its #[test] attribute — the exact shape reserve_bounded_retry_reports_conflict_when_takeover_is_blocked already uses in verbs/reservations/tests.rs:232. Change nothing else: not the assertions, not the production path, not any other test.

trace.outcome: the unix-only trust-file test is cfg-gated so the Windows crate compiles again

report.outcome: cfg(unix) on preflight_warns_and_proceeds_when_the_file_is_unwritable; Windows compile errors E0433/E0599 removed at the source
report.tests: cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml -p bee preflight_warns — green — 4 preflight tests are the only ones the attribute can affect; the Windows arm is a compile-only fix CI proves on push
deviations: Ran in the main checkout: release-blocking CI red, and no overlap with the live doctor-freshness-version reservations
